authorisedkeysmc.screen.first-run.body1:
This mod replaces traditional passwords with public key cryptography for authentication.

Notably, there is no password to remember, and no password to transmit to servers. Your key pairs are as safe as the rest of your files.

This mod does nothing unless it is also installed on the server!
authorisedkeysmc.screen.first-run.body2:
You will now create a new key pair. Advanced users may create multiple key pairs if they wish.

Proceed, then change the name if you want. You can optionally set a password if, e.g., multiple users use the same installation.

Lastly, click "Generate" to generate the key pair.

You should check that this server key is correct.

Do you wish to continue?
If so, the server key will be remembered for future log-ins.
You must enter the current password to decrypt the "%1$s" key pair, then either re-encrypt it with a new password, or leave it blank to keep the key pair unencrypted.

Do not forget your new password. Recovery is impossible without back-ups.
authorisedkeysmc.screen.wrong-server-key: changed since the last time you joined.
Usually, this means the server key was changed out by the admin (e.g. reinstalled). Rarely, it may mean the connection is being intercepted.
Please double-check that the key does indeed belong to the server.
By continuing, you trust the new server key, and it will replace the current one.
